name: Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth
funding: 2025-26 grants include Sid W. Richardson Foundation, Ben E. Keith Foundation, Bank of America Charitable Foundation, City of Fort Worth and Texas Commission on the Arts. Corporate: Frost, Headington Companies.
watch: Sid W. Richardson's oil fortune funds its foundation, which gave in 2025-26. Fort Worth police seized Sally Mann photographs in January 2025; no charges followed.
records_note: Names funders under a 2025-2026 grants heading but posts no annual report, accounts or board; Form 990 filings for 2001 to 2025 sit on ProPublica.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego
funding: Expenses $13.7M (FY2025); $40M+ endowment, trustees, banks (JPMorgan, Northern Trust, Bank of America), Westfield UTC, KPBS.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Corporate partner page not read. The corporate partner page and board were read and no excluded name appears. The 1990s pergola dispute was about architecture, not funding.
records_note: No annual reports found; audited statements 2016 to 2025 and Form 990s are on its site, corporate partners show as logos, and trustees are listed.

name: Craft Contemporary
funding: Expenses $1.9M (FY2025); Getty, Luce, Parsons foundations, LA city and county arts funds, First Citizens Bank, Sony Pictures, members.
records_note: No annual reports found; the FY2025 Form 990 is on its site, an Annual Donor Recognition list for 2025-26 names funders, and trustees are listed.

name: New Orleans Museum of Art
funding: Expenses $13.1M (2024); contributions 62%; trustees include Gayle Benson and Walda Besthoff (retail); First Horizon Bank.
watch: Flag rests on the Helis Foundation, funded by the William Helis oil family and a current sponsor of free admission. Besthoff, Zemurray and bank money is not flagged. The Taylor Energy founder's foundation is also listed in 2020.
why_flagged: Non-funding row: #DismantleNOMA racism claims (2020) and the June 2023 backlash over a curator hire. The current donor roster is unpublished (last one is 2019).
records_note: NOMA posts annual reports for 2011 to 2020, financial statements for 2011 to 2021, a donor list inside the 2020 report and its 2026 trustees.

name: Oakland Museum of California
funding: Expenses $20.4M (FY2025); City of Oakland subsidy, foundation trustees, members.
watch: Chevron and Bloomberg Philanthropies are current Benefactor-level corporate supporters, and the museum also uses Bloomberg Connects.
why_flagged: Chevron and Bloomberg Philanthropies are current Benefactor-level corporate supporters, and the museum also uses Bloomberg Connects.
records_note: It posts yearly Impact Reports, audited statements and Form 990s for 2021 to 2025, names corporate partners by tier and lists 2025/2026 trustees.

name: Palm Springs Art Museum
funding: Expenses $11.4M (FY2024); trustees, Bank of America, Sotheby's, Parker Palm Springs hotel, property firms, Pritzker for A+D.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Board not verified. Sept 2024: three trustees quit over the director hire; whistleblower alleged restricted endowment funds were misused (museum denies).
records_note: No annual reports; audited accounts and 990s for 2021 to 2024 are on its site, sponsors are undated logos, and the board is listed.

name: Heard Museum
funding: Revenue $23.2M (FY2025); trustees, Dickey family, members, Indian Fair.

why_flagged: Trustee Gregory H. Boyce is the former Peabody Energy (coal) executive chairman. Indian Fair sponsors include coal-burning utilities APS and SRP.

name: Nevada Museum of Art

name: Utah Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Revenue $2.1M, expenses $1.8M (FY2024-25); Salt Lake County ZAP, Utah Arts & Museums, IMLS, Warhol Fdn, Eccles fdns, Zions Bank.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Corporate sponsors unverified. Board president and $25k+ donor Rich Walje is ex-CEO of Rocky Mountain Power (coal-heavy utility).

name: McNay Art Museum
funding: FY2025 (year to June): endowment draw $2.15M (20% of $10.7M expenses), contributions $2.25M, memberships $0.56M, admissions $0.29M. No donor list found.
watch: Marion Koogler McNay's oil-wealth bequest (1950) is now a diversified endowment; its draw covers about 20% of expenses. No current oil donor is documented.
records_note: Its Financial Reporting page posts annual reports from 1998 to 2025, audited statements from 2013 and Form 990s, plus a 2022-23 donor list.
